title: Firm AI facts
description: What a small firm has confirmed about the AI tools it uses with client data. One answer per question; anything not confirmed stays an open point. Used by kit 2 (AI statement and answer letter) and meant for kit 3 (the AI section of client questionnaires): both read the same saved file.
rules: A sentence appears only for an answer the firm gave. No answer, or a 'not sure' answer, becomes an open point under 'What we are still checking'.
What the firm checked and what a vendor states are kept apart. Vendor statements come from the AI accounts guide, with their sources and check date.
No sentence calls a tool or the firm safe or compliant.

fields.label: Your firm's name
fields.hint: Used in the statement and the letter. It stays in your browser.

fields.label: Who clients can ask about it
fields.hint: A role or a shared address, for example "our office manager, privacy@yourfirm.nl".

fields.label: For your clients' data, what is your firm?
options: Their processor: we handle it for them under a processing agreement
Controller: we decide how we use it for our work
Both, depending on the client or the work

fields.label: Which AI accounts does the firm provide or allow for work?
fields.hint: Tick each account the firm arranged or agreed to. Then answer the short questions that appear for each one.

fields.label: Do you know which AI tools staff actually use, including their own accounts?
options: Yes: we checked in the past six months (survey, admin screens, billing)
We go by what the firm pays for

fields.label: Personal AI accounts (an employee's own ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude) for work
options: Allowed, but never with client data

fields.label: Which client data may go into the firm's AI tools?
options: None: only our own material and public information
Only with names and identifying details removed
Client data, in the work accounts only

fields.label: Sensitive data: BSN, health data, other special categories
options: Only where the client agreed in writing

fields.label: A client asks you not to use AI on their work
options: We agree with them how we work

fields.label: Does a person check AI output before it goes to a client?
options: Always, and whoever signs it off is responsible

fields.label: Do staff know the rules and the tools' limits?
fields.hint: The AI Act's Article 4 asks firms that use AI systems to see to their staff's AI literacy.
options: Briefed or trained, and kept up

fields.label: Are the AI vendors on the sub-processor list you give clients?
options: Not applicable: we are not a processor

fields.label: If client data goes into an AI tool by mistake
options: We have a procedure: record, assess, tell the client

processor.en: For our clients' data we usually act as their processor: we handle it on their behalf, under a processing agreement. An AI tool we use on that data is then a sub-processor.
processor.nl: Voor de gegevens van onze klanten zijn wij meestal verwerker: we verwerken ze namens hen, onder een verwerkersovereenkomst. Een AI-tool die we daarbij gebruiken, is dan een subverwerker.

controller.en: For our clients' data we act as controller: we decide how we use it for the work we do for them.
controller.nl: Voor de gegevens van onze klanten zijn wij verwerkingsverantwoordelijke: wij bepalen hoe we ze gebruiken voor het werk dat we voor hen doen.

both.en: Depending on the work, we act as our clients' processor or as controller. Where we are their processor, an AI tool we use on their data is a sub-processor.
both.nl: Afhankelijk van het werk zijn wij verwerker of verwerkingsverantwoordelijke. Waar wij verwerker zijn, is een AI-tool die we gebruiken op de gegevens van de klant een subverwerker.
